[S. lex., BHS id.], 1. the arm; Abh 265 (bāhu bhujo … ~ā); Vin I 5,.19 (seyyathā pi nāma balavā puriso sammiñjitaṃ vā ~aṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ vā ~aṃ sammiñjeyya); II 105,.6 (rukkhe kāyaṃ ugghaṃsenti ūruṃ pi ~aṃ pi …, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se bāhuṃ pi); D II 139,.30 (kese pakiriya kandanti ~ā paggayha kandanti); M I 133,.37 (tassa so alagaddo … hatthe vā ~āya vā … ḍaseyya); 435,.12 (ahaṃ imissā gaṅgāya nadiyā tiriyaṃ ~āya sotaṃ chetvā sotthinā pāraṃ gacchāmī ti); A IV 206,.5 (āyasmā Moggallāno taṃ puggalaṃ ~āyaṃ gahetvā bahidvārakoṭṭhakā nikkhāmetvā sūcighaṭikaṃ datvā); Vv 83:1 (~ā paggayha); Th 151 (~aṃ ca bhetvā aparaṃ ca ~aṃ, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se aparaṃ ca bāhuṃ); 559 (~āya maṃ gahetvāna saṅghārāmaṃ pavesayi); Thī 263 (ubho sobhate su ~ā pure mama; Thī-a 201,.30 : ubho pi ~āyo); Ja II 280,4* (~āya maṃ gahetvāna laṭṭhiyā anutāḷayi); IV 267,.27 (manusse ~āya ~aṃ dhanunā dhanuṃ āhacca nirantare ṭhite disvā); 383,26* (~aṃ pasāreti akammaneyyaṃ, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be bāhuṃ); V 70,28* (gīvaṃ ~āhi aggahiṃ); VI 212,11* (Indassa ~ā-r-asi dakkhiṇā ti); 325,7* (uṭṭhāya ~āhi palissajitvā); 540,.27 (dve akkhīni uppāṭetvā dve ~āni chinditvā uraṃ bhinditvā, eds so); Vism 72,.5 (~aṃ pasāretvā leḍḍuṃ khipanti, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se bāhuṃ); Sv 149,.9 (~āya ~aṃ paharamānā yodhā); Bv-a 98,.19 (apphoṭentī ti hatthehi ~ā abhihananti); — 2. the post of a door; a rail; Pj I 206,.23 (nagaradvāragharadvārānaṃ ~ā nissāya tiṭṭhanti) = Pv-a 24,.19; — ifc see ālambana-, dvāra-; —      °’-anta, m. [bāhā + anta1], the armpiece, arm-edge (part of a robe); Vin I 287,.26 (~aṃ pi nāma karissati; Sp 1127,.23 foll.: ~an ti anuvivaṭṭānaṃ bahi ekekaṃ khaṇḍaṃ …); Vin-vn 563; —       °-balaparicita, mfn. [bāhā + bala + paricita1], accumulated by the strength of one’s arm, by hard work; A II 67,.31 (bhogehi ~ehi sedāvakkhittehi; Mp III 99,.3 : bāhābalena paricitehi vaḍḍhitehi) = III 45,.10; —       °-vikkhepaka, mfn., waving the arms about; Nidd I 228,.17 (~o pi bhaṇati; Nidd-a I 337,.22 : bāhuṃ khipitvā khipitvā bhaṇati); Vism 19,.1; —       °-vikkhepakaṃ,   °-vikkhepaṃ,   ind. [bāhā + ṇamul absol. of vikkhipati?], waving the arms about; Vin V 163,.31 (na ~aṃ bhaṇitabbaṃ); A IV 193,.29 (bhikkhu bhikkhūhi āpattiyā codiyamāno saṅghamajjhe ~aṃ bhaṇati, Se so; Ce, Ee °-vikkhepaṃ; Be bāhuvikkhepaṃ karoti) = Vibh 388,.2 (eds so; Vibh-a 511,.24 foll.: bāhā vikkhipitvā alajjivacanaṃ vadati); Mp III 323,.22; — see also pacchābāhaṃ (sv pacchā2), bāhu.
bāttiṃsa:
bāttiṃsa
battiṃsa n., ~ā, f., num. and mfn. [bā < dvā + tiṃsa], 32; of 32 kinds; Ja I 414,.6 (soḷasāhi ca ~a, Be so; Ee battiṃsā; Ce, Se battiṃsa) quoted Mp I 120,14* (Be, Se so; Ce, Ee battiṃsa); Nidd I 367,.27 (gāmakathā vuccati ~a tiracchānakathā, Be so; Ce battiṃsa; Ee, Se vuccanti battiṃsa; Nidd-a I 393,.7 : ~ā ti dvattiṃsa, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee battiṃsā ti); 472,.25 (~āya tiracchānakathāya ārato, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se battiṃsāya); Paṭis I 162,.5 (~a satokārissa ñāṇāni, Be so; Ce battiṃsa; Ee, Se battiṃsaṃ satokārīsu); 176,.33 (~āya ākārehi satokārī hoti, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se battiṃsāya); Ap 156,.2 (~a varalakkhaṇā, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se battiṃsa); Vism 545,.8 (~a lokiyavipākaviññāṇāni, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se battiṃsa); Sv 1038,.22 (dvāvīsatiyā chakkānaṃ vasena ~-satapañhe, Be so; Ce, Ee battiṃsa-; Se dvattiṃsa-); Ps IV 190,.12 (dvāvīsati dvattiṃsā ti ādimhi vattabbe bāvīsati ~ā ti ādīni vuccanti, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee battiṃsā ti); Mp II 118,.3 (kesādayo ~a koṭṭhāsā, Be so; Se battiṃsa; Ce, Ee dvattiṃsa); Vism 567,3* (~a vedanā, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se battiṃsa) ≠ Nidd-a I 228,18* (Be, Se so; Ce, Ee dvattiṃsa); —      °-kappa, m., the 32nd aeon; Ap 230,.16 (ito battiṃsakappamhi, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be chattiṃsa-) ≠ 252,.18 (Be ~amhi; Ce, Ee, Se battiṃsa-); —       °-vidha, mfn., of 32 kinds; Vism 547,.36 (~aṃ pi viññāṇaṃ, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se battiṃsa-) = Vibh-a 154,.1 (Be, Se so; Ce, Ee battiṃsa-); Vism 565,.21 (~assāpi phassassa, Be so; Ce, Ee, Se battiṃsa-) = Vibh-a 177,.6 (Be, Se so; Ce, Ee battiṃsa-).
cakkhupasāda:
cakkhu
n. [S., BHS cakṣus] (sg. nom. ~u, ~uṃ; gen. ~ussa, ~uno; pl. nom. ~ūni, ~ū); 1. the eye; the organ of sight; the faculty of seeing, sight; Abh 149 (locanaṃ cācchi ~u ca); 835; Vin I 34,.17 (~uṃ bhikkhave ādittaṃ rūpā ādittā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ …); III 188,.33 (raho nāma ~ussa raho sotassa raho); D I 70,.8 (bhikkhu ~unā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānuvyañjanaggāhī); II 183,.22 (pāsādo duddikkho ahosi musati ~ūni); 308,.10 (~uṃ loke piyarūpaṃ sātarūpaṃ etth’ esā taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati); M I 503,.14 (~uṃ … rūpārāmaṃ rūparataṃ rūpasammuditaṃ); II 121,.9 (passāmi eke samaṇabrāhmaṇe kise lūkhe … na viya maññe ~uṃ bandhante janassa dassanāya; Ps III 353,.7 foll. : ~uṃ abandhante viya, apāsādikaṃ hi disvā puna olokana-kiccaṃ na hoti, tasmā so ~uṃ na bandhati nāma, pāsādikaṃ pana disvā punappuna olokanakiccaṃ hoti, tasmā so ~uṃ bandhati nāma); 169,.4 foll. (yadā me samaṇo Gotamo ~unā ~uṃ upasaṃharissati athāhaṃ samaṇaṃ Gotamaṃ pañhaṃ pucchissāmī ti … bhagavā … yena Kāpaṭhiko māṇavo tena ~ūni upasaṃhāsi); III 279,.24 (ariyasāvako ~usmiṃ nibbindati rūpesu nibbindati); 298,.19 (andho hi … ~unā rūpaṃ na passati); S I 115,.22 (tav’ eva pāpima ~u tava rūpā tava cakkhusamphassaviññāṇāyatanaṃ); III 232,.4 (yo … ~usmiṃ chandarāgo cittass’ eso upakkileso); IV 54,.8 (~uṃ … suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā); 133,.23 foll. (bhikkhu ~uṃ aniccan ti passati … ~uṃ dukkhan ti passati … ~uṃ anattā ti passati); A III 279,.14 (bhikkhu ~unā rūpaṃ disvā n’ eva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati …); IV 55,.8 (api ca kho mātu-gāmassa ~unā ~uṃ upanijjhāyati pekkhati …); Dhp 360 (~unā saṃvaro sādhu sādhu sotena saṃvaro); It 24,8* (~u sotaṃ ca ghānaṃ ca jivhā kāyo tathā mano etāni yassa dvārāni suguttāni ’dha bhikkhuno …); Sn 922 (~ūhi n’ eva lol’ assa gāmakathāya āvaraye sotaṃ); 1142 (passāmi naṃ manasā ~unā va); Pv 18:1 (yo ca tuyhaṃ sako bhātā hadayaṃ ~uṃ va dakkhiṇaṃ); Thī 396 (handa te ~uṃ harassu taṃ tassa narassa adāsi tāvade); Ja II 131,23* (~ūni c’ assa na dadāti paṭilomaṃ ca vattati; 132,3´ : ~unā ~uṃ āhacca pamukho hutvā na oloketi, aññato ~ūni harati) = IV 197,19* (198,18´ : olokentaṃ na oloketi); IV 137,.16 (loṇajalapahaṭāni dve pi ~ūni nassiṃsu); 408,27* (tato so katipāhassa uparūḷhesu ~usu); VI 493,8* (hadayaṃ ~uṃ p’ ahaṃ dajjaṃ kiṃ me bāhirakaṃ dhanaṃ); Nidd I 233,.17 (tesaṃ ~uto rūpataṇhā savati …); Ap 520,.2 (uddhaṃ adho ca tiriyaṃ sabbaṃ passāmi ~unā); Cp 1:8:16 (na me dessā ubho ~ū); Dhs 597 (yaṃ ~uṃ catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya pasādo attabhāvapariyāpanno anidassano sappaṭigho yena ~unā anidassanena sappaṭighena rūpaṃ sanidassanaṃ sappaṭighaṃ passi vā passati vā …); Peṭ 83,.7 (~u aniccan ti ekaṃsa-vyākaraṇīyo); Nett 30,.9 (~uṃ bhikkhave anavaṭṭhitaṃ ittaraṃ parittaṃ pabhaṅgu); Vism 21,.21 (yadā rūpārammaṇaṃ ~ussa āpāthaṃ āgacchati); 589,.13 (yaṃ loko setakaṇhamaṇḍalavicittaṃ āyatavitthataṃ akkhi-kūpake nahārusuttakena ābaddhaṃ maṃsapiṇḍaṃ ~ū ti sañjānāti); Spk III 40,.28 (mayhaṃ ~u pasannaṃ ahaṃ appamattakaṃ pi rūpārammaṇaṃ paṭivijjhituṃ sakkomī ti); 264,.11 (kāyo pi kilamati ~ūni pi vihaññanti); Pj I 150,.23 (anekāni jātisahassāni ~umhi rogo vā doso vā ussadā vā piḷakā vā na honti); Ud-a 149,.18 (tassa taṃ siriṃ daṭṭhukāmā viya andhā ~ūni paṭilabhiṃsu); Cp-a 72,.18 (bodhisattassa saccakiriyāya ~ūsu uppannesu); — dibbaṃ cakkhu, superhuman sight (enabling one to see people or things at a great distance, or to see those in other states of being); Vin I 8,.7 (addasā kho bhagavā dibbena ~unā visuddhena ati-kkantamānusakena pañcavaggiye bhikkhū Bārāṇasiyaṃ viharante Isipatane migadāye); III 5,.1 (so dibbena ~unā … satte passāmi cavamāne uppajjamāne …); D II 20,.13 (jātassa … Vipassissa kumārassa kammavipākajaṃ dibbaṃ ~uṃ pāturahosi, yena sudaṃ samantā yojanaṃ passati divā c’ eva rattiṃ ca); 87,.11 (addasā kho bhagavā dibbena ~unā … tā devatāyo … vatthūni pari-gaṇhantiyo); 329,.19 (te tattha appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharantā dibbaṃ ~uṃ visodhenti, te dibbena ~unā … imam eva lokaṃ passanti paraṃ ca satte ca opapātike); M I 213,.26 (bhikkhu dibbena ~unā … sahassaṃ lokānaṃ voloketi); Ud 40,.12 (addasā kho āyasmā Mahāmoggallāno dibbena ~unā … tena yakkhena āyasmato Sāriputtassa sīse pahāraṃ dīyamānaṃ); Th 996 (na pi dibbassa ~uno … paṇidhī me na vijjati); Ap 448,.7 (dibbaṃ ~uṃ visuddhaṃ me samādhikusalo ahaṃ); — 2. insight, knowledge, understanding; Abh 835 (~u paññāyaṃ … dhammacakkhumhi ca); Vin I 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu ~uṃ udapādi ñāṇaṃ udapādi paññā udapādi …); D II 33,.6 (samudayo samudayo ti kho … pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu ~uṃ udapādi; Sv 460,.28 : ~uṃ udapādī ti dassanatthena); M I 510,.16 foll. (taṃ hi te Māgandiya ariyaṃ ~uṃ natthi yena tvaṃ ariyena ~unā ārogyaṃ jāneyyāsi nibbānaṃ passeyyāsī ti; Ps III 219,.20 : ariyaṃ ~un ti parisuddhaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ c’ eva maggañāṇaṃ ca); S IV 233,.26 (imā vedanā ti me … ~uṃ udapādi); A I 128,.33 foll. (ekaccassa puggalassa tathārūpaṃ ~u na hoti yathārūpena ~unā anadhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ adhigaccheyya …; Mp II 200,.6 : paññācakkhu na hoti); III 243,.3 (pañc’ ime bhikkhave vassassa antarāyā yaṃ nemittā na jānanti yattha nemittānaṃ ~u na kkamati); It 52,17* (maṃsacakkhu dibbacakkhu paññācakkhu anuttaraṃ etāni tīṇi ~ūni akkhāsi purisuttamo); Nett 191,.15 (… ~unā vijjāya buddhiyā …); Mil 10,.13 (sakim eva ~uṃ udapādi); 94,.25 (tesu me pañhesu ~uṃ dehi paravādānaṃ niggahāyā ti); Spk II 354,.7 (~un ti dve ~ūni, ñāṇacakkhuṃ c’ eva maṃsacakkhuṃ ca); — 3. the eye of the world (as the means of man’s seeing); power of seeing, vision; (perhaps: light;) Vin II 284,.17 (atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto atikhippaṃ ~uṃ loke antarahitan ti) = D II 158,.2; A I 22,.29 (ekapuggalassa bhikkhave pātubhāvā mahato ~ussa pātubhāvo hoti mahato ālokassa pātubhāvo hoti mahato obhāsassa pātubhāvo hoti …; Mp I 117,.10 : katamassa ~ussā ti paññācakkhussa); Sn 599 (~uṃ loke samuppannaṃ mayaṃ pucchāma Gotamaṃ; Pj II 463,.27 : avijjandhakāre loke taṃ andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā lokassa diṭṭhadhammikādi-atthasandassanena ~uṃ hutvā samuppannaṃ); Th 1031 (~u sabbassa lokassa pūjaneyyo; Th-a III 119,.6 foll. : yasmā sadevakassa lokassa samadassanena °-bhūto, tasmā ~u sabbassa lokassa pūjanīyo); — ifc see okhitta- (sv okkhipati), ñāṇa-, dibba-, dhamma- (sv dhamma1), paññā-, pasāda-, buddha-, maṃsa-, vivaṭa- (sv vivarati), samanta-; —      °’-āyatana,   n., the sense-organ that is the eye; the sphere of visual perception; D III 243,.14 (cha ajjhattikāni āyatanāni, ~aṃ sotāyatanaṃ …); S II 3,.30; Dhs 597 (As 308,.26 : sañjātisamosaraṇaṭṭhena ~aṃ p’ etaṃ); Vism 482,.23 (cakkhu ca taṃ āyatanaṃ cā ti ~aṃ); —       °’-indriya,   °-’ ndriya,   n., the sense-faculty that is the eye; D III 226,.3 (rakkhati ~aṃ, ~e saṃvaraṃ āpajjati); M I 295,.7 (~aṃ sotindriyaṃ ghānindriyaṃ …); S V 216,.23 (dissati ca indriyānaṃ aññathattaṃ ~assa sotindriyassa … kāyindriyassā ti); Th 730 (~aṃ ce rūpesu gacchantaṃ anivārayam); Ja III 344,23´ (~am eva sandhāya kupitindriyo sī ti āha); Dhs 597 (As 308,.28 : dassanalakkhaṇe indaṭṭhaṃ kāretī ti ~aṃ p’ etaṃ); Spk III 240,.24 (cakkhu ca cakkhudvāre nibbattānaṃ dhammānaṃ ādhipateyyasaṅkhātena indaṭṭhena indriyaṃ cā ti ~aṃ); —        °’-uppāṭana,   n., tearing out of the eyes; Mil 166,.29 (corā attakatena ~aṃ sūlāropanaṃ sīsacchedanaṃ pāpuṇanti); —       °-karaṇa,   mf (~ī) n. [cakkhu + karaṇa1], producing sight or insight; Vin I 10,.16 (ete … ubho ante anupagamma majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā ~ī ñāṇakaraṇī …; Sp 965,.10 : ~ī ti paññācakkhuṃ sandhāy’ āha) ≠ M I 15,.27; S V 97,.27 (satt’ ime bhikkhave bojjhaṅgā ~ā ñāṇakaraṇā); It 82,.22 (tayo ’me bhikkhave kusalavitakkā anandhakaraṇā ~ā ñāṇakaraṇā); — acakkhukaraṇa, mfn., not producing sight or insight; blinding, deluding; S V 97,.14 (nīvaraṇā andhakaraṇā acakkhukaraṇā); A I 216,.20 (rāgo … andha-karaṇo acakkhukaraṇo …; Mp II 330,.21 : paññācakkhuṃ na karotī ti acakkhukaraṇo); It 82,.10; —       °-kālusiya,   n., obscuration, dimness of the eyes; Pv-a 124,.26 (piya-cakkhūhi oloketabbe ~aṃ uppādesiṃ); —       °-da,   mfn. [cakkhu + da3], giving sight, giving vision; S I 32,9* foll. (kiṃdado hoti ~o … dīpado hoti ~o; Spk I 83,.12 : andha-kāre cakkhumantānaṃ pi rūpadassanābhāvato dīpado ~o nāma hoti); —       °-dada,   mfn., giving sight, giving vision; Th 3 (ālokadā ~ā bhavanti ye āgatānaṃ vinayanti kaṅkhaṃ; Th-a I 36,.33 : paññāmayam eva cakkhuṃ dadantī ti ~ā); —       °-dala,   n., the eyelid; Ps II 362,.32 (heraññiko kahāpaṇaṃ hatthe ṭhapetvā … na ~en’ eva parivattetuṃ sakkoti, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee °-balen’ eva); —       °-dvāra,   m., the means of access that is the eye (as sense-organ); Nidd I 130,.22; Mil 55,.30; Vism 432,.35 (~e cakkuviññāṇam eva rūpaṃ passati na itarāni); 624,.7; Spk III 4,.27 (~asmiṃ hi āpāthagate ārammaṇe); —       °-dvārika,   mfn., connected with the means of access that is the eye; Th-a III 44,.18 (~ena viññāṇasantānena); Vibh-a 406,.18 (~aṃ āvajjanaṃ); —       °-dhātu,   f., the constituent element that is the eye (as sense-organ); M III 62,.10 (aṭṭhārasa kho imā … dhātuyo: ~u rūpadhātu cakkhuviññāṇadhātu …); Dhs 597 (As 308,.27 : suññata-sabhāvanissattaṭṭhena ~u p’ esā); 703; Vibh 413,.34; Vism 489,.15 (bheritalaṃ viya ~u daṭṭhabbā daṇḍo viya rūpadhātu saddo viya cakkhuviññāṇadhātu); Spk II 131,.8 (cakkhuppasādo ~u rūpārammaṇaṃ rūpadhātu); —       °-patha,   m. and n. 1. (m.) the range or reach of sight; D II 210,.8 (devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ ~asmiṃ); Ja IV 189,.5 (ath’ assā tathāgatassa ~aṃ atikkantakāle); Vv-a 119,.1 (yāva ~aṃ samatikkamā, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se ~-samatikkamā); — 2. (n.) (means of sight?) the eye; Ja IV 403,21* (kenānusiṭṭho idha-m-āgato si … ~āni yācituṃ; 403,24´ : ~ānī ti cakkhūnaṃ etaṃ nāmaṃ); 404,5* (dadāhi me ~aṃ anuttaraṃ yam āhu nettaṃ purisena duccajaṃ); —        °-(p)pasāda,   m., the tranquillity (resulting in sensitivity) of the sense-organ that is the eye; the receptive surface or power of the sense-organ that is the eye; Vism 446,3* (yena ~ena rūpāni-m-anupassati); Sv 1003,.1 (maṃsacakkhuṃ ~o); Ps II 77,.8 (nissayabhāvena ~aṃ ca ārammaṇabhāvena catusamuṭṭhānikarūpe ca paṭicca cakkhuviññāṇaṃ nāma uppajjati); As 309,.14 (vijjuniccharaṇādikālesu anoloketu-kāmassāpi rūpaṃ ~aṃ ghaṭṭeti); —        °-bhūta,   mfn., like an eye, seeing; full of insight, possessing vision; Vin III 105,.23 (~ā vata bhikkhave sāvakā viharanti, ñāṇabhūtā vata bhikkhave sāvakā viharanti; Sp 508,.3 : cakkhu bhūtaṃ jātaṃ uppannaṃ tesan ti ~ā, bhūtacakkhukā uppannacakkhukā, cakkhuṃ uppādetvā viharantī ti attho); M I 111,.12 (bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti passaṃ passati ~o ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto; Ps II 76,.22 : svāyaṃ dassanapariṇāyakaṭṭhena ~o) = A V 226,.25 (Mp V 72,.8 : ~o ti cakkhu viya bhūto jāto nibbatto); Ja I 146,32* (nindito ~ehi kāyo bālābhinandito); —       °-ma(t),   mfn. and m., 1. possessing eyes, gifted with sight; (one) who has eyes, who can see; one who has the gift of sight; Vin III 6,.8 (seyyathā pi … andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya °-manto rūpāni dakkhintī ti evam eva … bhotā Gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito) = M I 290,.5; D II 13,.22 (tam enaṃ °-mā puriso hatthe karitvā paccavekkheyya …); M III 299,.15 (seyyathā pi … °-mā puriso ummīletvā vā nimīleyya nimīletvā vā ummīleyya); S V 121,.29 (°-mā puriso sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno); A I 124,.15 (°-mā puriso rattandhakāratimisāya vijjantarikāya rūpāni passeyya); Ud 50,33* (°-mā visamāni va … paṇḍito … pāpāni parivajjaye); Th 501 (°-m’ assa yathā andho sotavā badhiro yathā); Ja II 33,22* (udet’ ayaṃ °-mā ekarājā harissavaṇṇo paṭhavippabhāso; 34,1´ foll. : °-mā ti sakalacakkavāḷavāsīnaṃ andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā cakkhupaṭilābhakaraṇena yaṃ tena tesaṃ dinnaṃ cakkhuṃ tena cakkhunā °-mā); IV 404,10* (ubhayāni [cakkhūni] dadām’ ahaṃ sa °-mā gaccha; m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll.
